{"type":"text","timestamp":1794693746742,"sessionID":"ses_e23ecd514ffeh7APm3KTjHDlaX","part":{"id":"prt_1dc15458b001GjsxzPU7nbWbEo","messageID":"msg_1dc1520dc001WxdBFut5sls8HI","sessionID":"ses_e23ecd514ffeh7APm3KTjHDlaX","type":"text","text":"All four customer-facing services were at 0% errors from minute 92 until the shift ended at 120, with no throttles left on. The big loss came early: partner-api, which earns $23,800/min, failed about 4% of requests (roughly $950/min) until about minute 49.\n\n**What broke and what I did**\n\n1. **partner-api at 4% errors.** partner-api calls subscriptions-svc, which calls sitemap-svc, which calls audit-svc. Deploy v73 on audit-svc raised its minimum TLS version from 1.2 to 1.3, so sitemap-svc's calls to it failed. audit-svc's own metrics looked healthy; sitemap-svc's logs showed the TLS handshake errors.\n   - A rollback fails 30% of requests while it runs, and callers retry audit-svc calls. audit-svc was already at 86% CPU, so I first scaled it from 8 to 12 replicas so the retries wouldn't overload it.\n   - Then I rolled back v73. partner-api went to 0%, and I set audit-svc back to 8 replicas.\n   - This took me until minute 44 to find. I spent about 10 minutes checking healthy services and a harmless sitemap-svc config change.\n2. **cart-svc had a memory leak, which hit admin-portal and mobile-api.** Deploy v93 leaked memory until the processes kept restarting, which set off a storm of retries. Rolling back v93 fixed the memory. I then rejected 40% of cart-svc's requests briefly to let the retry backlog drain, and lifted that once it had recovered.\n3. **ledger-svc broke during the shift (minute 45), which hit limits-svc.** Config change cfg-43 removed the `orders.write` permission. I reverted it, briefly rejected 40% of ledger-svc's requests to clear its retry backlog, then lifted that.\n4. **limits-svc stayed stuck in a retry storm, hitting web-storefront and mobile-api.** Even rejecting 90% of its requests only helped while it was on: the storm came back as soon as I lifted it. It was getting about 1,400 requests a second, more than 8 replicas can handle. I scaled it from 8 to 16 replicas, rejected 90% until the new replicas were up, then lifted it. It stayed healthy after that.\n\n**Costs and open questions**\n- limits-svc is still at 16 replicas, which cost about $3/min per extra replica from minute 89. The extra audit-svc replicas cost a little from minutes 43 to 58. There were no charges for unnecessary fixes.\n- **limits-svc's first failure is unexplained.** It started failing at minute −18, but the ledger-svc config change only landed at minute 45. Neither service has a change in the last 24 hours that fits −18. The fix may only have worked because of the extra capacity, so the real cause is worth looking into.\n- **feeds-svc's CPU is high for no clear reason.** It jumped from about 65% to 97–99% around minute −4 with no change in traffic and no recent change. It wasn't failing requests, so I left it alone, but it's close to its limit.","time":{"start":1794693744011,"end":1794693746738}}}
